title: Audit Partners’ Role in Material Misstatement Resolution: Survey and Interview Evidence

scopes.description: The as-downloaded PDF-only release, assessed for the documented survey and interview workflow. The proposal's manual recruitment, survey, and interview stages are credited as research workflow; they do not supply executable analysis code or establish which planned stages were completed.

requirements.description: The author-prepared respondent-level survey data needed to reproduce the documented ranking/comparison of response options and cross-sectional analyses. The datasheet says the final dataset came from the Qualtrics survey portal, but this release contains no response file. The required export schema, response labels, missing-value handling, exclusions, and any derived variables remain unspecified.

A deidentified participant/invitation and response summary sufficient for the proposal's early/late response comparison and respondent-versus-invited-pool firm-size/generalizability checks, including the relevant dates or response-order field, contact mode, eligibility, participant characteristics, and denominator values. Do not assume personal names or email addresses are needed in a shared file.

The proposal calls for comparing respondents' background, experience, specialization, and demographic characteristics with partners covered by AuditAnalytics. The frozen catalog returns auditor firm/entity and change/event candidates; AUDIT.FEED89_PCAOB_REPORT exposes aggregate partner/staff counts, not a demonstrated individual-partner profile. The exact source product/table, population unit, required fields, identifier map, reference period, and compatible access route remain unverified. This firm-level count candidate is not treated as a substitute for the named partner-level comparison.

The proposal includes selected pre-survey quotations drawn from nine transcripts, but no separate full transcripts or transcript/quote-selection files appear in the assigned inventory. The proposal also describes post-survey coding and planned deviant-case/quote checks in future tense; which stages were later completed is unresolved. Participant confidentiality is described, but current sharing permission or a restriction is not established.

issues.description: The package inventory contains only two PDF documents and no executable program. The documentation does provide a substantive manual/Qualtrics survey and interview workflow, but it does not include the computer program or a detailed step-by-step processing recipe that produces the final analysis data.

The datasheet describes ranking and comparing survey response options, and the proposal outlines cross-sectional and nonresponse checks, but the supplied documents do not specify exact data preparation, calculations/tests, result-generation steps, software, or the mapping from the Qualtrics export to analyzed variables. These are concrete workflow gaps, not proof that a data source is restricted.

The supplied paper text labels itself a 2021 JAR Registered Reports Conference Proposal and describes survey and post-survey interview stages in future tense. Its title matches the frozen title, so no attribution conflict is inferred; however, the package does not establish which planned stages or analyses were completed for the frozen paper target.

evidence.quote:
Consistent with the best practices in interview-based qualitative research in accounting, we

intend to interview approximately 10 additional partners and 10 CFOs and ACMs or until

additional interviews provide little incremental benefit (Malsch and Salterio 2016). In selecting

partner participants for interviews, we will strive to have our interview sample resemble our survey

participants (Nelson and Skinner 2013). We will also select CFOs and ACMs from companies that

resemble those audited by our survey respondents to ensure that the interviewees speak to the same

issues as those considered by our partner respondents in the survey (Miles et al. 2018). We also
evidence.description: The proposal describes planned follow-up interviews with partners and CFOs/audit-committee members, selected to resemble the survey context.

evidence.quote:
We will take several steps to increase the credibility of the post-survey interview responses

(Nelson and Skinner 2013; Miles et al. 2018; Malsch and Salterio 2016; Lune and Berg 2017; Yin

2018). First, we will code the post-survey interviews to systematize and discipline quote selection.

Second, we will examine our post-survey interview data for potential inconsistencies with our

results by conducting deviant case analysis and disclosing material exceptions to notify readers

about the boundaries of the inferences that can be drawn from our findings. 18 Last, we will share

the manuscript with the interviewees to verify that the quotes we used accurately represent their

statements. Importantly, the participants will not be granted the right to veto anything in the paper.
evidence.description: The proposal describes coding post-survey interviews, deviant-case analysis, and interviewee quote verification.

review_notes: Frozen title and DOI metadata are preserved. The proposal's printed title matches the frozen title; its conference-proposal label and future-tense survey/post-survey interview descriptions are retained as stage/version uncertainty, not an attribution conflict or evidence that planned stages were completed.

The release's two PDFs provide a substantive research workflow: the survey instructions and instrument, manual participant-pool and invitation description, Qualtrics survey administration and respondent comparisons, nine completed pre-survey interviews with selected transcript-derived quotations, and a planned post-survey interview coding/deviant-case/quote-review process. This is workflow and prepared-document evidence, not executable analysis code.

The datasheet says the final survey dataset came from Qualtrics and that two authors would retain data/programs for six years. The assigned inventory contains no response export, participant/invitation frame, AuditAnalytics input, transcript files, or program; no separate analysis-only scope is supported.

The frozen catalog lookup for AuditAnalytics returned 54 candidates. The selected metadata includes auditor identity/change feeds and a PCAOB report table with aggregate partner/staff counts; it does not establish a compatible person-level partner-profile input, data-file readability, historical coverage, or current access. No underlying table or data rows were read.

The datasheet marks its proprietary-source disclosure item not applicable. This does not establish current user access or unrestricted permission to share survey or interview records; no NDA, license, or confidentiality barrier is inferred. The interview materials must be considered under their actual consent terms.

No analysis software or executable statistical procedure is named in the supplied text. Qualtrics is identified as survey-administration software, not as evidence of a verified analysis runtime. No software dependency is inferred.
